sources.name: Megalodon (Emergent)

sources.name: Skeleton Ship (Fleet)
sources.notes: The regular ships of a Skeleton Fleet (waves one to three, one or two ships each). A smaller loot pool than the emergent skeleton ships and never any smuggler goods.

sources.name: Skeleton Captain

sources.name: Skeleton Lord
sources.notes:
Reskins with the same loot: The Two-Faced Scoundrel, The Duchess, The Mutinous Helmsman. Portrait: The Two-Faced Scoundrel.
Final boss of Skeleton Fort and Reaper Fortress.

skeletons-orders.notes: Quest item dropped by Skeleton Captains during a Fort of Fortune (leads to a skeleton voyage). Wiki: seaofthieves.wiki.gg/wiki/Skeleton%27s_Orders

sources.name: A Legendary Search for the Skull of Destiny
Reaper Fortress
sources.notes: Two vaults. The Weapon Cache opens with the Skull of Arms dropped by the Master of Arms in one of the waves (the skull also sells to the Smugglers' League); the Fort Vault opens with the fort key.

sources.name: Skeleton Ship (Smugglers)
sources.notes: Looks exactly like a regular skeleton ship but carries the Smugglers' League loot pool (paintings, chronicles, rum, black powder) on top of the regular one. Fleet ships are never smuggler ships.

sources.name: Ghost Fleet
sources.notes: Waves of Ashen Dragon ships, then two grunt ships with Flameheart's ship. Sink the two grunts before the final ship: once the boss ship goes down the grunts despawn and their loot is lost.

sources.name: Ghost Fleet

sources.name: Megalodon (Emergent)
sources.notes: The megalodons that roam the seas (not the Megalodon Hunt voyage). Every colour variant - Hungering One, Crested Queen, Shadowmaw, Ancient Terror - drops the same loot. The Ancient Megalodons (Barnacled Dread, Feared Redmaw) are a different type.
